title: Glossary of the convention
description: The terms the documents use, each with the section that defines it. The documents own the definitions; these entries point at them.

entities.title: Mark
entities.summary: One of ✅, ⚠️, ❌ and ⛔ on a statement in documentation, saying whether the statement is true of the system yet.
notToBeConfusedWith: Mention: the same glyph in a legend, an example, a template or a quotation, which is not a claim
A status icon in the product, such as a badge on an admin page; marks never go in a string a user reads

entities.title: Mention
entities.summary: A glyph that is not a claim about the system: a legend, or a mark inside an example, a template or a quotation.
notToBeConfusedWith: Mark: a claim about the system, which the greps are meant to find

entities.title: Graduation
entities.summary: When a document has no ⚠️ and no ❌ left, every ✅ in its body is deleted and its status line is replaced by one line saying it is fully implemented, tested and free of known defects.

entities.title: Knowledge document
entities.summary: A Markdown document describing the system as it should be, in the present tense, from one named perspective, each statement about a capability carrying a mark.
notToBeConfusedWith: Knowledge file: in human-assisted software development, a structured .dev/<kind>.json file next to the code, such as the files in this repository's .dev folders

sources.symbol: 4. Write the documents that are missing

entities.title: Deferred-work gate
entities.summary: The gate that fails the build on a TODO, FIXME, HACK or XXX marker opening a comment in a tracked source file, and on any tracked path under a TODO/ directory; the one rule that needed a build failure.
notToBeConfusedWith: The optional gates (graduation, orphan-⛔, legend and Markdown TODO checks), none of them serious if missing

entities.title: Change log
entities.summary: A file written for every prompt that changes the code base: what was asked for, how the agent interpreted it, and what the change needs (testing, data migration, compatibility).
notToBeConfusedWith: The changelog: the record of the past that stays alongside the documents and, like decision records, never carries marks
